title: Hrehaan Roshan, Hrithik's Son, Makes Music Debut With Indie Single From Berklee
excerpt: The 20-year-old Berklee scholar releases 'This Heavenly Place,' an acoustic English-language track that marks the first independent music career from the Roshan family
body:
• Hrehaan Roshan, the 20-year-old son of Hrithik Roshan and Sussanne Khan, has released his debut single 'This Heavenly Place' as an independent artist
  • The acoustic indie-pop track, performed in English, was written, composed and sung by Hrehaan, who also plays guitar on it
  • Hrehaan is studying at Berklee College of Music in Boston on a scholarship, making him the first singer-songwriter from the Roshan family
  • Hrithik Roshan, Sussanne Khan, Saba Azad and grandfather Rakesh Roshan all publicly celebrated the debut on social media
  • The Roshan family's musical lineage traces back to Hrehaan's great-grandfather Roshan, a celebrated Hindi film composer, and grand-uncle Rajesh Roshan

Hrehaan Roshan has stepped out from behind one of Bollywood's most recognizable surnames to launch a music career on his own terms. The 20-year-old son of actor Hrithik Roshan and designer-entrepreneur Sussanne Khan released his debut single, This Heavenly Place, on August 28 across Spotify, YouTube and Apple Music.

It is not a Bollywood playback debut. There is no film attached, no label fanfare, no choreographed launch event. Instead, the track is a stripped-back, acoustic indie-pop song in English — a 3-minute, 36-second meditation on young love that Hrehaan wrote, composed, sang and played guitar on himself. The black-and-white music video matches the minimalism: just Hrehaan, his guitar and a microphone.

A Berklee Scholar, Not a Star Kid

Hrehaan, who goes by the stage name "hrehaan" and is called "Ray" by his family, developed an interest in music during his teenage years in Mumbai. He began learning guitar and writing songs before pursuing formal training at Berklee College of Music in Boston, where he earned a scholarship and is currently completing an undergraduate degree.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=CZNfiWfn0OU

His musical influences reportedly span Hindi film music and Western rock and alternative — a combination that makes sense given his upbringing. But the debut leans firmly toward the Western indie side, with no trace of Bollywood orchestration or Hindi lyrics.

"You were born with an innate wisdom Ray: I trust it so much. It makes me fearless."

— Hrithik Roshan, on social media

The Roshan Musical Lineage

Music runs deep in the Roshan family, though it has historically expressed itself through film rather than independent artistry. Hrehaan's great-grandfather, Roshan — born Roshan Lal Nagrath — was a prominent Hindi film composer whose work remains part of the Bollywood canon. His grand-uncle, Rajesh Roshan, composed the soundtrack for Hrithik's blockbuster debut film Kaho Naa... Pyaar Hai (2000).

Hrehaan's choice to perform under a mononym — "hrehaan" — is said to be a nod to his great-grandfather, who was similarly known by a single name. But the musical direction is distinctly his own: indie-pop rather than film scores, English rather than Hindi, independent release rather than studio backing.

With this debut, Hrehaan becomes the first singer-songwriter and guitarist from the Roshan lineage to pursue music as an independent artist rather than through the film industry.

Family Celebrates

The release drew an immediate wave of support from the extended Roshan family on social media. Hrithik Roshan shared the track on Instagram Stories, writing about his trust in his son's creative instincts. Sussanne Khan commented under the music video: "Sooooooo overwhelmed love u beyonddddddd anytime."

Saba Azad, Hrithik's partner and herself an independent musician, wrote: "So so beautiful Ray. So proud of you." Grandfather Rakesh Roshan, the filmmaker behind the Krrish franchise, offered his blessing: "Ray so proud of you, keep soaring."

The production on This Heavenly Place was handled by Sudan, with Ankur Tewari — a well-known indie musician and A&R figure in Indian music — credited for artist and repertoire duties on the project.

Charting His Own Course

Hrehaan's debut arrives at a moment when the children of Bollywood stars face intense public scrutiny over whether they will follow their parents into film. His younger brother Hridhaan, 18, has not indicated a career direction. Hrithik and Sussanne married in 2000 and divorced in 2014; both have been publicly supportive of their sons' individual paths.

By choosing music over movies, and an independent acoustic single over a Bollywood launch, Hrehaan has signaled that his relationship with the family legacy will be on his own terms. Whether This Heavenly Place finds a wide audience remains to be seen — but the first notes are his alone.
